quote: In this episode, Phil Nadel, managing partner of Forefront Venture Partners, shares his journey from angel investing to running one of the largest rolling funds on AngelList.
claim: The article introduces Nadel as Forefront Venture Partners’ managing partner and an AngelList rolling-fund manager.

quote: So yeah, it's just been, you know. an evolution of businesses over the years that eventually led me to become a VC investor and put founding companies sort of on the back burner.
claim: Nadel says his entrepreneurial career eventually led him to become a VC investor.

quote: So at the time that we exited, we were at about 130 million in annual revenue. And it was a good exit for us, worked out really well.
claim: Nadel says the publishing company he operated with his father had about $130 million in annual revenue when they exited it.

quote: I started doing that for family and friends only and on a small scale.
claim: Nadel says his investing began on a small scale with family and friends.

quote: Why don't we team up and launch a syndicate, which we did. And, it, it took off. I mean, it really did, grew very quickly in terms of the number of LPs.
claim: Nadel says he and Barbara Corcoran launched an investment syndicate that grew quickly.

quote: Barbara never really played an active role. She's more of a passive partner with me. And she's not involved at all in sort of the investment decision -making or anything like that.
claim: Nadel describes Barbara Corcoran as a passive syndicate partner who was not involved in investment decisions.

quote: and then ultimately launching our own fund in the form of a rolling fund, which we did about three years ago, which is also managed on the Angel list platform.
claim: Nadel says they subsequently launched a rolling fund managed through AngelList approximately three years before this interview.

quote: When I say the fund, I'm the GP, so I make the decisions along with our investment committee.
claim: Nadel says he serves as the fund’s GP and makes investments with its investment committee.

quote: And we don't charge any management fees or upfront fees either. It's only the carried interest.
claim: Nadel says the rolling fund charges carried interest but no management or upfront fees.

quote: Well, there are four of us who are sort of full -time and then there are a bunch who are part -time and then we have all these ad hoc advisors. So four full -time though.
claim: Nadel describes the investment operation as having four full-time team members plus part-time personnel and ad hoc advisers.

quote: We try to do a post -mortem, if you will, on companies whose investments didn't work out.
claim: Nadel says Forefront performs post-mortems on unsuccessful investments.

quote: we really go above and beyond by introducing potential customers to our, to the founders of our portfolio companies by introducing a talent to them when they're recruiting, by helping them make strategic connections, whether that's a reseller or technology partner, that kind of thing.
claim: Nadel says Forefront helps portfolio founders with customer, recruiting, reseller, and technology-partner introductions.

quote: We're going to require the companies we invest in to provide regular updates, monthly or quarterly updates that are detailed and provide KPIs and provide a request for assistance and give us thorough detailed information.
claim: Nadel says Forefront requires portfolio companies to provide detailed monthly or quarterly updates containing KPIs and requests for assistance.

quote: Grove Collaborative is one that you mentioned. They're a public company now trading on the New York Stock Exchange. We got involved at the very early stage, their seed round.
claim: Nadel says Forefront invested in Grove Collaborative at its seed round and that the company later traded publicly on the New York Stock Exchange.

quote: Another public company that we invested in very early on is called Zoom Car.
claim: Nadel says Forefront invested in Zoom Car very early.

quote: We invested in the meditation app, Calm, which I could use more of.
claim: Nadel says Forefront invested in Calm.

quote: Peerspot, which is based in Israel, has also done very, very well. So there are so many that I'm proud of, some of which we've exited, some that we're still holding.
claim: Nadel names Peerspot among successful portfolio companies while stating generally that Forefront had exited some named investments and still held others, without specifying which category included Peerspot.

quote: The company you mentioned, Assure Health, he just recently exited. They were very, very successful and sold the company and he's still involved, but he's moved on to his next venture.
claim: Nadel says his son Jeff recently exited Assure Health after its sale but remained involved; this describes Jeff’s relationship, not a Forefront investment.

quote: Unfortunately, not. No allocation. And there's a reason behind that, as you can imagine. We try to maintain a Chinese wall between us.
claim: Nadel says Forefront received no allocation in his son’s ventures and maintains separation to avoid a conflict.

quote: I'll give you a few examples of companies we invested in prior to COVID that by all accounts should have been decimated by COVID, but were not. One is a company based in Chicago called Party Slate.
claim: Nadel identifies Chicago-based Party Slate as a Forefront investment made before COVID.

quote: But PartySlate, because they understood the pain points that their customers were facing and because they morphed their product and and evolved so quickly in reaction and response to COVID. They were able to actually grow during COVID, which is remarkable.
claim: Nadel reports that portfolio company PartySlate adapted its product during COVID and grew during that period.

quote: Open Reel is another that took advantage of COVID and in terms of their business because they provide a remote video solution.
claim: Nadel identifies Open Reel as another portfolio company and says its remote-video business benefited during COVID.

quote: I guess one other company I would point out that just off the top of my head that was impacted by COVID was a company called BluffWorks, which is an apparel company that makes travel related apparel gear.
claim: Nadel identifies apparel company BluffWorks as a portfolio company affected by COVID.

quote: Again, they change their messaging a little bit and their branding to focus more on comfort and style and ease of use for the products.
claim: Nadel reports that BluffWorks responded to COVID by changing its messaging and branding.

quote: you can go to forefrontvp.com, that's our website, forefrontvp.com. I'm very present on LinkedIn, so Phil Nadel, you can go to my profile on LinkedIn and connect with me there.
claim: Nadel identifies ForefrontVP.com as the firm’s website and the Phil Nadel LinkedIn profile as his social profile.

quote: We respond to all emails. And so we don't mind cold outreach.
claim: Nadel says Forefront accepts cold outreach and responds to all emails.
